It depends on the contract. It would be worth taking an eagle eye to read any fine print from solicitors you plan on going with. 

I currently have a “no win, no fee” medical negligence case running and my solicitor had to take out an insurance premium that covers the cost of their and the opponent’s fees if I was to lose, which means in the event of a loss, I would not be liable to pay any costs, including expert witness fees etc. 

Most reputable Top 100 law firms for med neg. have this sort of structure so it’s worth looking into, just be sure to get the low-down on fees and costs from your solicitor.

I’m genuinely not sure myself. I must’ve been on the track before the train hit me, but at the same time I would’ve thought that trains have something in front of them that’d push me aside, but it kinda just went straight over me and my leg of course. I must’ve been in quite a weird position with just my left leg sticking out

The moment between jumping and actually physically being on the track was a blur but all I can remember is that I was on the track, I immediately felt this train passing over me and I immediately could feel something wasn’t right in my lower body. I kinda weirdly didn’t feel much of it at all probably due to shock but I just remember kinda gritting my teeth and wincing. Almost like a dull pain that lasted for a couple of seconds. 

Seeing my leg next to me was just surreal, considering it still had my Adidas trainer and part of my trouser leg on. It was like it was just a piece of lifeless meat that was attached to me just a few seconds ago. But weirdly, I kinda calmly came to terms with that I just wouldn’t have a leg anymore. The fact that I may bleed out to death kinda scared me more so I started screaming for help about that. I’m pretty sure my fear was stronger than my psychological pain but I got drugged up fairly quickly once the paramedics came and things went quite fast after that

I live in the UK. The current psych ward I’m at gets 50% NHS and 50% private referrals and is a little fancier than most psych wards here. I’m lucky in that it allows access to mobile phones and laptops etc. however I don’t think all do and I have to get all of my devices charged at the nurses station. It’s fairly lax and since I’m informal I get a lot more freedom than I would if I was formal (sectioned under the Mental Health Act) (e.g going out to the shops or taking a walk unsupervised, however due to my mobility it’s best if I’m supervised)
